concerns.rationale: The FIDO reference continues the preceding footnote; its materials are not supplied. It cannot resolve the unidentified second duty or edition uncertainty.
This begins the hardware-security-key explanation, continued in units 134–137. Storage examples do not identify or establish performance of the second duty.
The hardware examples and storage description depend on adjoining footnote text. They supply no gift rule or second-duty performance test.
Hardware credentials are described as device-local and unsynchronised, with FIDO2/WebAuthn protocols. Preserve that distinction from synchronised managers; neither original question is resolved.
This continues the explanation of hardware credential retention and interception risk. It is not a standalone measurable performance criterion or proof of duty performance.
The protection statement completes the hardware-key footnote. It supplies no quantitative acceptance threshold and does not resolve the second duty.
This begins the separate explanation of ecosystem passkey managers. It must be read with units 139–142 and the synchronisation controls in units 175–177.
Synchronisation is described across trusted ecosystem devices. This does not dispense with the later controls against unauthorised access or establish second-duty performance.
Named managers are examples within a continuing footnote, not independent approvals or a complete authentication standard. The original question mapping remains unsupported.
Multi-device sign-in describes manager functionality; it must remain subject to synchronisation-risk controls. It does not establish that any duty has been performed.
This completes the passkey-manager protection explanation. It supplies no operational acceptance threshold and cannot resolve either original question.
This is a repeated address, not a substantive duty. The synthetic dependency and second-duty mapping remain unexplained.
This is the repeated Chinese address. Its normative metadata does not establish a legal obligation or resolve the synthetic concern.
Contact and website details provide document context, not a gift prohibition or second-duty performance criterion.
The page marker preserves document order but supplies no duty. It does not resolve edition uncertainty or the synthetic mappings.
This begins the illustrative new-client setup scenario, completed by units 148–152. It cannot be treated as a universal compulsory passkey route.
Platform alternatives and onboarding timing continue across units 147–152. This fragment does not independently define the second duty.
First-time setup is part of the new-client illustration and depends on the identity-verification condition in unit 150. No performance facts are supplied.
Successful completion of required identity verification precedes the passkey prompt. The content and adequacy of those steps remain judgment-dependent and are not established here.
The passkey-creation prompt follows identity verification in the new-client illustration. It does not prove implementation or make passkeys the only acceptable method.
This completes the account-linking phrase in units 147–151. It has no independent gift or second-duty meaning.
The illustration concerns existing clients with bound devices. Preserve the separate unit 13 exception against requiring existing clients to rebind already-bound devices.
This route assumes a bound device and an application supporting passkey authentication. Those conditions cannot be inferred for all clients or used to establish duty performance.
The existing login process precedes the creation prompt in this bound-device scenario. This does not authorise all existing authentication processes indefinitely.
This completes the bound-device client's passkey-linking illustration. It neither requires rebinding nor identifies the original second duty.
This distinct scenario is limited to existing clients without bound devices during the implementation period. The timing qualification must survive the partition boundary.
The platform list continues the time-limited scenario in unit 157. It cannot be detached from the implementation-period qualification.
Existing credentials are part of the transitional illustration continued in units 160–161. They do not establish an enduring exception to robust authentication.
SMS OTP appears only in the implementation-period illustration begun in unit 157. Preserve that temporal limit and the interim enhanced monitoring and immediate protective-action requirements.
Device binding is qualified by applicability in this transitional passkey scenario. It must not become a universal rebinding requirement for existing clients.
This begins the separate post-implementation scenario for existing clients without bound devices. Preserve its distinction from units 157–161; the original duty remains unidentified.
Post-period passkey creation calls for robust verification, with examples continued in adjoining units. Robustness has no complete executable acceptance criterion in the proposal.

Identity and biometric verification examples include a paragraph 7 cross-reference whose target is not clearly identified in the supplied appendix. Retain that dependency rather than silently repairing it.
An in-person office visit is an alternative in the post-period passkey-creation scenario. Preserve the alternative and unresolved cross-reference; neither establishes actual performance.
This completes the post-period passkey-creation scenario. Its conditions and alternatives reside in units 162–165 and cannot be discarded.
Comprehensive policies, procedures and controls for passkey revocation and recovery are a separate expectation. A login or date predicate would not account for this duty.
Revocation and recovery cover multiple credential-storage arrangements, continued in units 169–170. No supplied proposal establishes adequate management or performance.
Loss, compromise and replacement are distinct circumstances within the recovery-control expectation; inaccessibility follows in unit 170. Preserve all circumstances.
This completes the inaccessibility circumstance in units 167–169. It is not a standalone duty or a basis for either original Boolean answer.
Client guidance for lost or compromised authentication storage is a separate expectation, continued in units 172–174. It cannot be absorbed into a generic authentication-compliance fact.
The guidance covers security keys and managers as well as bound devices and introduces an additional verification condition. Its adequacy and performance remain unresolved.
Appropriate identity verification must precede passkey creation, revocation or recovery. Preserve all three operations and the sequencing; appropriateness requires judgment.
This completes the passkey verification clause and connects it to the following synchronisation controls. It cannot stand alone as a performance test.
Appropriate controls for synchronised software passkeys are a distinct expectation. The proposal supplies neither a defined adequacy test nor implementation facts.
The synchronisation-control expectation concerns multiple client devices and continues into unit 177. Manager functionality described earlier is not evidence that this expectation is met.
Preventing abuse of synchronisation is an outcome expectation without supplied testing or performance thresholds. It cannot be represented by an opaque overall-compliance fact.
This heading introduces device binding, a distinct authentication route. It does not identify which obligation the original second-duty question means.
This begins the device-binding description, completed in units 180–184. The association alone does not establish robust enrolment or duty performance.
Securely enrolled device attributes qualify the association between platform and client device. Preserve this condition across the partition boundary; actual enrolment security remains unknown.
The description explains verification of login origin using enrolled attributes. It does not replace robust initial binding or the additional login factor described in the circular.
Prior registration to the client's account is part of device-origin verification. It does not prove legitimate registration or satisfaction of all authentication expectations.
Reduced reliance on credentials describes a security benefit, not an independent acceptance threshold. The second duty and its performance remain unidentified.
This completes the description of mitigating access from unregistered devices. It does not prohibit every unbound-device interaction, including the later robust binding examples.
This starts the warning about weak verification at device binding. Read through units 186 and 191–193 despite intervening page furniture; the warning does not establish performance.

Credentials and OTP-based binding are identified as vulnerable, with the sentence continuing after page furniture. Preserve the implementation-period qualification elsewhere without treating OTP as phishing-resistant.
This repeated address interrupts a continuing substantive sentence. It creates no independent duty and does not resolve the synthetic concern.
This repeated Chinese address is page furniture. Preserve substantive continuity from units 185–186 to 191–193; the original question mapping remains unresolved.
Repeated contact details have no independent authentication obligation or gift rule. Their presence cannot substantiate second-duty performance.
This page marker does not break the weak-verification warning or establish edition validity. The synthetic concern remains unresolved.
This resumes the warning about phishing-induced unauthorised registration and introduces the resulting expectation. Preserve its connection to units 185–186 and 192–193.
Robust verification for binding is an expectation for internet brokers and VASPs, not distributors dealing with gifts. Adequacy, timing and actual implementation remain separate unresolved issues.
The stated purpose is reducing account takeover and unauthorised registration. It does not supply a quantitative robustness criterion or identify the second duty.
This heading introduces the binding standards that follow. It supplies no standalone performance test and does not repair either original question.
The introductory should governs the following binding standards. Preserve that modality and the actual regulated actors; the original second-duty prohibition classification is unsupported.
Robust registration and linking methods are required by the continuing standard in units 196–200. Preserve the existing-device exception and do not infer that every client must rebind.

The authentication-method clause continues in units 198–200 with alternative or additional verification controls and confirmation of device ownership before registration. Do not truncate that alternative at this batch boundary.

questions.rationale: Retained as an original question, but the supplied source concerns internet-trading cybersecurity and supplies no gift prohibition. The distributor, gift assessment unit and prohibition meanings lack source support. No Boolean answer or executable proposal is justified.

Retained separately. The second duty is unidentified, and its performance question conflicts with its gift-prohibition result kind and truth meanings. The source contains multiple distinct duties and no evidence of their actual performance. Selecting one authentication or timing predicate would not account for the others.

remaining_uncertainty: The supplied earlier reading expressly proposes no legal interpretation and has null formalization. No replacement interpretation or executable result is proposed; revised_interpretation is null.

All 263 source units were considered as context. This response disposes only of the 66 selected concerns for units 132–197; it does not revise other batches or complete the whole-source reconciliation.

The synthetic mappings from every unit to gift.question and unit 262, and from each concern to second.duty and unit 0, do not establish legal dependencies. Unit 262 completes the physical-verification example, including additional identity proof where appropriate; it is not a universal condition for every source unit.
Preserve the exception that existing clients need not rebind already-bound devices. It does not exempt new registrations, replacement-device binding, login controls or other duties.

The supplied text requires robust authentication as soon as practicable and no later than 8 July 2027, with immediate implementation expected for large internet brokers. The meaning of large, operational immediacy, practicability and the exact temporal boundary remain unresolved; the final date alone cannot establish compliance.

Preserve the distinction between existing clients with bound devices, those without bound devices during the implementation period, and those without bound devices afterward. Transitional OTP use does not make OTP phishing-resistant or displace enhanced monitoring and immediate suspension or restriction upon suspicious activity.

Passkeys and bound devices are examples, with platform suitability, two-factor authentication, strong registration verification, FIDO certification for passkey solutions, lifecycle controls and synchronisation controls remaining relevant. Device-binding standards retain phishing-resistant methods and/or additional verification controls; the supplied illustrations must not be converted into an exhaustive list.

Robustness, appropriate certification and verification, adequate testing, comprehensive controls and prevention of synchronisation abuse require further assessment. No quantitative performance thresholds or implementation evidence are supplied.

The appendix's reference to paragraph 7 is not clearly matched by the supplied numbered text. Five dependencies have missing source hashes, and referenced external materials are not supplied in full. Edition and dependency uncertainty remain open.

Notification, surveillance, incident response and reporting, client education, management oversight, implementation testing, rollout, client support and notification of anticipated deadline difficulty remain separate expectations with their own qualifications and timing. No narrow authentication predicate resolves them.
Question inventory remains a proposed interpretation. No gift prohibition, duty-performance finding, overall-compliance fact or unknown fact value has been inferred.
